questions.title: Fuel Cost Estimator
questions.description:
A road-trip planner estimates how much fuel money a drive needs: litres used = distance / mileage and cost = litres * price. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double fuel_cost(double distance, double mileage, double price)

It must return distance / mileage * price. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the distance in km, the mileage in km per litre, and the price per litre.

Output Format:
One line with the estimated fuel cost rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= distance <= 5000, 1 <= mileage <= 50, 1 <= price <= 200

questions.title: Seconds to Clock Parts
questions.description:
A timer converts a raw second count into hours, minutes and seconds. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void to_clock(int total, int &h, int &m, int &s)

It must store total / 3600 into h, (total % 3600) / 60 into m and total % 60 into s. Do it with arithmetic only — no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the total seconds.

Output Format:
One line with h, m and s space-separated.

Constraints:
0 <= total <= 86399

questions.title: ATM Note Split
questions.description:
An ATM pays out using only 500- and 100-rupee notes, giving as many 500s as possible. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void split_notes(int amount, int &fives, int &hundreds)

It must store amount / 500 into fives and (amount % 500) / 100 into hundreds. Amounts are always multiples of 100 — arithmetic only, no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the amount.

Output Format:
One line with the count of 500-notes, then the count of 100-notes, space-separated.

Constraints:
100 <= amount <= 100000, amount % 100 == 0

questions.title: Digit Sum of a Three-Digit Code
questions.description:
A checksum routine sums the digits of a three-digit code. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int digit_sum3(int n)

It must return the sum of the three decimal digits of n. Arithmetic only — no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the integer n.

Output Format:
One line with the digit sum.

Constraints:
100 <= n <= 999

questions.title: Swap via References
questions.description:
A sort utility needs an in-place swap helper built on C++ references. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void swap_ints(int &a, int &b)

It must exchange the values of a and b using a temporary. Do not call std::swap — write the exchange yourself.

Input Format:
One line with two integers.

Output Format:
One line with the two values after the swap, space-separated.

Constraints:
-1000 <= values <= 1000

questions.title: Roll Number Prefix and Digit
questions.description:
A roll-number validator strips the last digit off a registration number. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void last_digit(int n, int &prefix, int &digit)

It must store n / 10 into prefix and n % 10 into digit. Arithmetic only — no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the roll number n (at least two digits).

Output Format:
One line with the prefix, then the last digit, space-separated.

Constraints:
10 <= n <= 999999

questions.title: Electricity Slab Bill
questions.description:
A utility bills electricity in slabs: the first 100 units cost 3 rupees each, the next 100 units cost 5 rupees each, and everything beyond that costs 8 rupees each. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int slab_bill(int units)

It must return the total bill for the given units. Use conditionals only — no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the number of units consumed.

Output Format:
One line with the bill in rupees.

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 10000

questions.title: Tiered Auto Fare
questions.description:
An auto-rickshaw meter charges a flat 25 rupees for the first 2 km, then 12 rupees per additional km. Rides longer than 10 km add a 20-rupee night surcharge on top. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int auto_fare(int km)

It must return the total fare for a ride of km kilometres. Conditionals only — no loops.

Input Format:
One line with the ride distance in whole kilometres.

Output Format:
One line with the total fare.

Constraints:
1 <= km <= 100

questions.title: Grade Classifier
questions.description:
An exam system maps an integer score to a letter grade:
90-100 → A, 75-89 → B, 60-74 → C, 40-59 → D, below 40 → F. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string grade_of(int score)

It must return the grade as a string ("A", "B", "C", "D" or "F").

Input Format:
One line with the score.

Output Format:
One line with the grade letter.

Constraints:
0 <= score <= 100

questions.title: Triangle Type Classifier
questions.description:
A geometry tool classifies a triangle from its three side lengths:
EQUILATERAL when all sides are equal, ISOSCELES when exactly two sides are equal, SCALENE otherwise. The input always forms a valid triangle. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string triangle_type(int a, int b, int c)

It must return one of the three strings above.

Input Format:
One line with the three side lengths.

Output Format:
One line with EQUILATERAL, ISOSCELES or SCALENE.

Constraints:
1 <= a, b, c <= 1000

questions.title: Phone Bill with Slabs
questions.description:
A telecom plan has a 99-rupee rental that includes 100 free minutes. Minutes 101-200 cost 0.80 rupees each, and every minute beyond 200 costs 1.20 rupees. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double phone_bill(int minutes)

It must return the total bill in rupees. Conditionals only — no loops. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the minutes used.

Output Format:
One line with the bill rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= minutes <= 10000

questions.title: Sum of Two Integers
questions.description:
Write and run your first C++ function. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int sum_two(int a, int b)

It must return the sum of a and b.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B.

Output Format:
One line with A + B.

Constraints:
-1000 <= A, B <= 1000

questions.title: Difference and Product
questions.description:
Practise C++ reference parameters: an out-parameter is an int& the function fills in. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void diff_prod(int a, int b, int &diff, int &prod)

It must store (a - b) into diff and (a * b) into prod. The harness prints both values for you.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B.

Output Format:
One line with A - B, then A * B, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= A, B <= 100

questions.title: Average of Three Doubles
questions.description:
Read and compute with double values. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double average_three(double a, double b, double c)

It must return (a + b + c) / 3. The harness prints the result rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with three numbers A, B and C.

Output Format:
One line with the average rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
-1000.0 <= A, B, C <= 1000.0

questions.title: Rectangle Area and Perimeter
questions.description:
Fill two out-parameters with the geometry of a rectangle. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void rect_props(double len, double wid, double &area, double &perim)

It must store len * wid into area and 2 * (len + wid) into perim. The harness prints both rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the length and the width.

Output Format:
One line with the area, then the perimeter, space-separated, each rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0.1 <= len, wid <= 1000.0

questions.title: Percentage of Marks
questions.description:
Mixed-type arithmetic: integer marks must be converted so the division is floating-point. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double percent(int marks, int total)

It must return marks * 100.0 / total. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: marks obtained and total marks.

Output Format:
One line with the percentage rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= marks <= total <= 1000

questions.title: Quotient and Remainder
questions.description:
Use C++ integer division and modulo through reference out-parameters. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void div_mod(int a, int b, int &quot, int &rem)

It must store a / b into quot and a % b into rem.

Input Format:
One line with two integers A and B (B is never zero).

Output Format:
One line with A / B, then A % B, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= B <= A <= 10000

questions.title: Simple Interest Calculator
questions.description:
A bank clerk computes simple interest: principal P, annual rate R percent and T years give P * R * T / 100. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double simple_interest(double p, double r, int t)

It must return p * r * t / 100. The harness prints the value rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the principal, the annual percent rate and the number of years.

Output Format:
One line with the simple interest rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
1 <= p <= 1000000, 1 <= r <= 20.0, 1 <= t <= 30

questions.title: Grocery Receipt Total
questions.description:
A checkout adds tax to a line item: the subtotal is price * quantity and tax is taxPercent percent of the subtotal. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    double receipt_total(double price, int qty, double taxPercent)

It must return price * qty * (1 + taxPercent / 100). The harness prints the total rounded to 2 decimals.

Input Format:
One line with the unit price, the quantity and the tax percent.

Output Format:
One line with the receipt total rounded to 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0.1 <= price <= 10000.0, 1 <= qty <= 1000, 0 <= taxPercent <= 50

questions.title: Cinema Ticket Cost
questions.description:
A multiplex charges 250 rupees per adult ticket and 120 rupees per child ticket. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int ticket_cost(int adults, int kids)

It must return adults * 250 + kids * 120.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: the number of adults and the number of children.

Output Format:
One line with the total ticket cost.

Constraints:
0 <= adults, kids <= 50
